statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of six representative paths. Excluded: authenticated post-observation/photo submission and forum content because they require credentials or are a separate host; duplicate weather/model templates were represented by the selected observation, city forecast, and AROME paths.

paths.description: Homepage and weather dashboard, representing the global shell, navigation, current conditions, consent entry state, and primary content overview.
Real-time observations listing/map, representing the main live-data browsing archetype.
City forecast search and Paris result, representing the primary forecast lookup form and completion flow.
AROME model map/index, representing dense model and image-heavy specialist pages.
Account sign-in, included because authentication, autofill, and secure account handling are high-risk contextual checks.
Deliberately invalid route, representing HTTP failure and recovery behaviour.

findings.summary: The interface does not honour the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually identical to the light capture: the content and consent surface remain light, and the DOM/CSS probe found no adaptive theme mechanism.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Auto-animated imagery continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe confirmed the preference but still found the animated satellite GIF anim_ir_small.gif and other GIF resources, with no reduction mechanism.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace nonessential animated GIFs with controlled media and show a still frame under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: Navigation and state changes are abrupt.
findings.evidence: The DOM/CSS probe found no view-transition usage across the global shell; navigation is a dense set of conventional full-document swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigation, while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: The extensive navigation chrome does not respond to scroll position.
findings.evidence: The full-page screenshots show a large persistent left navigation, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, progress indicator, or shrinking-header treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive, scroll-aware navigation cues where they improve orientation, without adding more chrome.

findings.summary: Dense navigation provides weak attention and location cues.
findings.evidence: Across homepage, observations, forecast, and model probes there is no H1; hundreds of similarly styled links compete with page content and state changes have no directional cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one clear page heading, current-location state, and stronger hierarchy for the active task.

findings.summary: A large consent interstitial obscures the core weather content on every fresh page load.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots on four archetypes show the same modal-like panel covering most of the content before interaction. A reject/continue link exists, but the interruption still dominates the entry state.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact consent surface that keeps core content usable, with equally prominent accept and reject choices.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is not exposed as a native dialog.
findings.evidence: The overlay visibly behaves modally, but the DOM probe found zero dialog, popover, or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the modal flow with <dialog>, correct focus management, Escape handling, and declarative dismissal.

findings.summary: Application chrome crowds out the weather content.
findings.evidence: The screenshots show a fixed 950px table shell, a very long left menu, many borders, tiny controls, and competing panels; at mobile size the entire desktop composition is scaled down.
findings.suggestedFix: Restructure around the core forecast/observation tasks, progressively disclose specialist links, and remove repetitive borders and menu noise.

findings.summary: The mobile page is a scaled-down desktop canvas rather than a usable responsive layout.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 capture renders a roughly 992px layout at scale 0.36. Layout evidence reports no viewport meta and a 992px CSS viewport; the DOM probe also sees 992px content against a 780px default viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a standard viewport meta tag and replace the fixed 950px table shell with fluid, intrinsically sized layouts that reflow at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Reusable panels do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no container queries or logical properties, while the same fixed shell is used across forecast, observation, login, and model archetypes.
findings.suggestedFix: Define reusable content/sidebar components and use container queries where their layout depends on available space.

findings.summary: Touch targets are too small even though keyboard focus is visible.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse target-size failed and the mobile screenshot shows densely packed, tiny navigation links; the focus probe did confirm a 1px browser outline on the first link.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive target size and spacing to at least 24x24 CSS px (prefer 44px for primary touch controls) while retaining focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: The primary weather tasks are buried in a dense, heading-free interface.
findings.evidence: The home probe found no H1, 263 links, and only sidebar H3 headings; the first viewport gives comparable weight to menus, ads/search, maps, observations, and models.
findings.suggestedFix: Establish a clear page title and prioritize current weather, location search, and forecast as the main actions; move specialist navigation behind clear groups.

findings.summary: Mobile Largest Contentful Paint is slow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 6.05s (performance 0.76), outside the 2.5s good threshold, although CLS was 0.0015 and TBT 22ms. The unthrottled trace measured LCP 2.66s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reduce render-blocking styles and third-party startup work, and verify under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Render-blocking and cache delivery delay primary content.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 950ms render-blocking savings and 497KiB cache-lifetime savings. HAR confirms seven parser-inserted stylesheets and 918KB transferred across 60 requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, consolidate/defer noncritical styles, and set effective cache lifetimes for versioned static assets.

findings.summary: Substantial unused JavaScript and third-party code ships on first load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 218KiB unused JavaScript. HAR shows scripts account for 435KB transferred, led by roughly 202KB of ad implementation code.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load advertising/consent functionality and remove unused first-load JavaScript.

findings.summary: Many controls, maps, images, and form fields lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: axe found 178 image-map areas without alternative text, 9 exposed images without alt, 2 unlabeled controls, 2 unnamed links, and an untitled iframe. The image primitive counted 29 images without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide labels and names for every field/control, useful alt for meaningful images/map areas, empty alt for decoration, and a descriptive iframe title.

findings.summary: Some text fails WCAG AA contrast.
findings.evidence: axe found two definite serious contrast failures and 135 additional nodes requiring review; Lighthouse’s colour-contrast audit also failed.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt tested text/surface tokens that meet WCAG AA in normal, dark, and high-contrast conditions.

findings.summary: Document structure is not a coherent heading and landmark hierarchy.
findings.evidence: The probe found no H1, no main/header/footer landmarks, and only sidebar H3s; axe reports 22 regions outside landmarks and malformed definition-list structure.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic header/nav/main/footer landmarks and a logical H1-to-H2 heading hierarchy; preserve visible focus order.

findings.summary: Text is too small and cramped, especially on mobile.
findings.evidence: The 360px screenshot scales the desktop layout to roughly 36%, making navigation, tables, and weather values illegible without zoom.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive type and spacing, shorter line lengths, and layouts that reflow rather than scale down.

findings.summary: The page fails mobile reflow and target-size expectations.
findings.evidence: There is no viewport meta; Lighthouse flags viewport and target-size problems, and the 360px capture shows the full fixed-width site compressed into one screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable user scaling, add the viewport meta, reflow at 320 CSS px, and enlarge touch targets.

findings.summary: Image and document asset hygiene is weak despite a valid doctype/charset.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 92 of 95 images without both dimensions, 95 legacy-format images, and one oversized image; Lighthouse also flags incorrect aspect ratio and unsized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image dimensions, preserve intrinsic aspect ratios, and modernize substantive imagery with responsive sources.

findings.summary: The page cannot use BFCache and Chrome reports inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found Cache-Control: no-store prevents BFCache restoration and its inspector-issues audit failed, although no deprecated APIs or console errors were reported.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove no-store where user-specific sensitivity does not require it and resolve DevTools Issues panel diagnostics.

findings.summary: Some controls are uncrawlable and the site lacks a mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found onclick-only region links without href; the DOM has five anchors without href and no viewport meta. robots.txt itself is valid.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for in-page state changes, real href links for navigation, and add the standard viewport meta.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The public homepage returns 200 but has no rel=canonical. robots.txt advertises HTTP sitemap text files, while /sitemap.xml returns the site’s HTML 404 document.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish canonical URLs and a valid HTTPS sitemap index, then reference that exact URL from robots.txt.

findings.summary: The public weather site lacks structured and social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and zero Open Graph tags on the homepage, despite its clear organization/weather-data identity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite structured data and Open Graph/Twitter preview metadata matching visible content.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP and cookie security are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers show HSTS and nosniff but no CSP. Two Matomo cookies are not Secure, including a 393-day identifier.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing CSP and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with proportionate lifetimes and SameSite policy.

findings.summary: Third-party advertising and analytics dominate much of the initial transfer.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 54 of 60 requests and 700KB of 918KB transferred to non-main origins; tracker evidence identifies DoubleClick, and scripts include Matomo and consent tooling.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize pre-consent collection, self-host or remove nonessential dependencies, and load advertising only after a valid consent choice.

findings.summary: The account flow is password-only and lacks modern autofill metadata.
findings.evidence: The login probe found a password form with no WebAuthn/passkey support and empty autocomplete values. No permission prompt appeared on initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Add autocomplete=username/current-password immediately and offer passkeys as a phishing-resistant sign-in option.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced security policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers lack frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy in addition to CSP; HSTS and nosniff are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP frame-ancestors, a strict Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: French pages do not declare their language and layouts are not writing-mode resilient.
findings.evidence: All representative probes report an empty html lang; the CSS probe found no logical properties. The site visibly serves locations beyond France.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang=fr and dir=ltr, then migrate directional layout properties to logical equivalents and prepare translated labels.

findings.summary: Locale-sensitive presentation is fixed to French without explicit locale semantics.
findings.evidence: Rendered weather dates and labels are French while html has no language and the inspected markup exposes no locale selector or Intl-based client formatting.
findings.suggestedFix: Define supported locales and format dates, numbers, and units with Intl APIs or equivalent locale-aware server formatting.

findings.summary: Weather times are presented without clear time-zone context.
findings.evidence: The homepage renders observation/update times such as 21:50 for geographically varied data, but no visible zone indicator or machine-readable time semantics were found in the representative DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Label time zones and use unambiguous machine-readable timestamps, converting for the selected station or user locale.

findings.summary: Forecast and sign-in inputs omit autofill assistance.
findings.evidence: The forecast and login probes found no autocomplete tokens on city, username, or password inputs.
findings.suggestedFix: Add appropriate autocomplete tokens such as address-level2/postal-code, username, and current-password.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not proportionately optimized.
findings.evidence: All 95 inspected images use PNG/GIF/JPEG-era formats, 84 below-fold images are eager, 92 lack dimensions, and responsive sources are largely absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold content, reserve dimensions, and use responsive modern formats for substantive imagery while retaining tiny icons where appropriate.

findings.summary: Third-party and animated-media cost is high relative to the core weather task.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 700KB and 54 requests; ad code alone is about 240KB, while an animated satellite GIF transfers about 100KB and continues under reduced motion.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, defer ads/analytics, and replace autoplay GIF delivery with controlled, cached media.

taskList.title: Rebuild the fixed-width shell as responsive, semantic, accessible UI
Make core weather content primary and remove the blocking consent experience
Reduce third-party collection and deploy browser security policies
Improve LCP and first-load resource delivery
Modernize image delivery, sizing, and media budgets
Add clear headings, active location, and guided navigation
Repair canonical, sitemap, crawlable-link, and share metadata
Declare language and make weather data locale/time-zone aware
Fix browser platform and document asset hygiene
